title: Data policies (DLP) for Copilot Studio agents
summary: The page's policy automation needs correction: Get-DlpPolicy retrieves policies but does not configure connector groups. The changed connector-classification documentation otherwise supports the page's explanation, including its warning about nonblockable connectors.

claims.where: summary; What it is; Why it matters
claims.claim: Power Platform data policies govern Copilot Studio agents in the environments within their scope.
claims.quote: These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope.

claims.claim: The Power Platform admin center path is Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Next > Add an environment > Next > Assign connectors.
claims.quote: Select Next. The Add an environment page appears. ... Select Next. The Assign connectors page appears. ... To prevent agent makers from using the features associated with the connector, select Block.
claims.fix: The path reaches the correct page but stops before the blocking control. For blocking, extend it to 'Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Next > Add an environment > Next > Assign connectors > connector > Block'. Keep Business and Non-Business classification described as assignments on the Assign connectors page.

claims.claim: Get-DlpPolicy is the automation shown for the control deciding connector and channel Business, Non-Business or Blocked assignments.
claims.quote: Retrieves a list of DLP policy objects. ... The Get-DlpPolicy cmdlet retrieves policy objects for the logged in admin's tenant.
claims.fix: Replace controls[0].api.call and the rendered call with 'Set-DlpPolicy -PolicyName <policy name> -UpdatedPolicy $UpdatedPolicy' and its docs with https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powerapps.administration.powershell/set-dlppolicy. Replace 'Automation shown lists policies only' with 'Updates the policy using the policy update object'. Add that reference and https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/data-loss-prevention-sdk to sources; the SDK documents updating a policy to move connectors across groups. Get-DlpPolicy may remain described only as a retrieval command, not as the automation that sets this control.

claims.claim: Tenant-level data policies require the Power Platform Administrator role.
claims.quote: To follow the steps described in this article for tenant-level policies, sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator role.

claims.claim: Environment-level policies require Environment Admin permissions when the environment has no Dataverse database.
claims.quote: To follow the steps for environment-level policies, you need to have Power Apps Environment Admin permissions.

claims.claim: Environment-level policies require System Administrator for an environment with a Dataverse database.
claims.quote: For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.

claims.claim: Add all environments applies a policy tenant-wide.
claims.quote: Add all environments: Adds all the environments in your entire tenant. This policy automatically applies to any new environment created in the tenant.

claims.claim: Get-DlpPolicy lists policies only.
claims.quote: Retrieve a list of data policy objects ... Get-DlpPolicy ... Gets policy objects for the signed-in admin's tenant.

claims.claim: Endpoint configuration is under Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Next > Add an environment > Next > Assign connectors > connector > Configure connector > Connector endpoints in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Select Next. The Assign connectors page appears. ... Select the three dots (⋮) next to the connector ... Select Configure connector > Connector endpoints.

claims.claim: New-PowerAppDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations -TenantId <tenant ID> -PolicyName <policy GUID> -NewDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations $ConnectorConfigurations configures policy endpoint rules.
claims.quote: PolicyName refers to the unique GUID. ... New-PowerAppDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations -TenantId $TenantId -PolicyName $PolicyName -NewDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations $ConnectorConfigurations

claims.claim: Maker guidance is reached through Copilot > Settings > Copilot Studio > Maker guidance > environment or environment group > Edit setting in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Under the Copilot Studio section, select Maker guidance. ... select the environments or environment groups ... Select Edit setting at the bottom of the panel ... A panel for configuring a custom message opens.

claims.claim: Custom Maker guidance messages can be configured for environments and environment groups.
claims.quote: You can configure different messages for different environments and environment groups to tailor guidance by governance zone.

claims.claim: The environment group guidance message overrides the environment message.

claims.claim: Custom guidance messages support plain text only.

claims.claim: A data policy sorts connectors into data groups and determines which connectors apps, flows and agents may use together.
claims.quote: The key point is that connectors in the same group can share data in Microsoft Power Platform, whereas connectors in different groups can't share data.

claims.claim: Learn also calls these data loss prevention (DLP) policies.
claims.quote: The policies that define how data can be shared are referred to as data loss prevention (DLP) policies.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/prevent-data-loss to sources for the DLP terminology. No wording change is needed.

claims.claim: The three connector data groups are Business, Non-Business and Blocked.
claims.quote: The three data groups are the Business data group, the Non-Business data group, and the Blocked data group.

claims.claim: A connector is assigned to one data group within a policy.
claims.quote: Connectors can reside in only one data group at a time.

claims.claim: Connectors in different data groups cannot share data.
claims.quote: You can't share data among connectors that are located in different groups.

claims.where: What it is: SharePoint and Gmail example
claims.claim: An app or flow cannot combine SharePoint in Business with Gmail in Non-Business.
claims.quote: If you place SharePoint and Salesforce connectors in the Business group and you place Gmail in the Non-Business group, makers can't create an app or flow that uses both the SharePoint and Gmail connectors.

claims.claim: A Blocked connector cannot be used where the policy applies.
claims.quote: Blocked connectors can't be used where this policy is applied.

claims.claim: Data policy enforcement has been in effect for all tenants since early 2025.
claims.quote: Since early 2025, data policy enforcement is in effect for all tenants

claims.claim: Agents cannot be exempted from data policy enforcement since March 2025.
claims.quote: Since March 2025, agents can't be exempted from data policy enforcement. It's no longer possible to exempt agents with a PowerShell command.

claims.claim: Virtual connectors are not based on REST APIs.
claims.quote: Virtual connectors are connectors that appear in data policies for administrators to control, but they're not based on a RESTful API.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio exposes capabilities through virtual connectors so data policies can govern agent features.
claims.quote: Microsoft provides several virtual connectors for governing Microsoft Copilot Studio. These connectors facilitate the ability to turn off various features of agents.

claims.claim: New connectors normally enter the policy's designated default group, initially Non-Business.
claims.quote: You must designate one data group as the default group to automatically classify any new connectors ... Initially, the Non-Business group is the default group for new connectors and all services.

claims.quote: If Microsoft adds any new connectors that can't be blocked and you set the default group for the data policy as Blocked, these connectors are automatically marked as Non-Business instead of Blocked.
